verdict.outcome_basis: readout: "Results of the Incremental Decrease in End Points Through Aggressive Lipid Lowering (IDEAL) study were presented today at the annual meeting" (announcement:ideal)

report.headline: The IDEAL trial (atorvastatin 80 mg vs simvastatin 20–40 mg in 8,600–10,000 CHD patients) missed statistical significance for major coronary events (HR 0.89, p=0.07) because the active-comparator design produced only a 0.59 mmol/L between-arm LDL-C difference, yielding a predicted 13.5% RRR (HR 0.865) for which the trial had only ~50–60% power.
report.summary: IDEAL compared intensive atorvastatin with standard simvastatin in secondary-prevention CHD patients. The between-arm LDL-C reduction was 0.59 mmol/L (18.85%), far smaller than statin-vs-placebo trials (~1 mmol/L), predicting a modest 13.5% relative risk reduction (expected HR 0.865). The observed HR of 0.89 matches this prediction almost exactly, but with only ~970 events (implied by p=0.07) against the 1,498 needed for 80% power, the trial was underpowered for the effect size its design could deliver. No safety signal or execution flaw explains the result; the genetics flag ('uncertain') reflects only a pre-2005 evidence cutoff, not a true mechanistic gap. The differential diagnosis confidently identifies effect_too_small (primary) and design_or_endpoint (secondary) as the drivers.
key_evidence: Between-arm LDL-C difference 0.59 mmol/L (atorvastatin −41 mg/dL vs simvastatin −18 mg/dL) predicting 13.5% RRR (expected HR 0.865) — New Lipitor Study Demonstrates that Intensive LDL Cholesterol Lowering in Heart Disease Patients Can Reduce Cardiovascular Events, Pfizer Says
Observed HR 0.89 (p=0.07) matches expected HR 0.865 — New Lipitor Study Demonstrates that Intensive LDL Cholesterol Lowering in Heart Disease Patients Can Reduce Cardiovascular Events, Pfizer Says

1,498 events needed for 80% power; ~970 events implied by p=0.07/HR=0.89 → ~50–60% power — Calculator, New Lipitor Study Demonstrates that Intensive LDL Cholesterol Lowering in Heart Disease Patients Can Reduce Cardiovascular Events, Pfizer Says

Active comparator (simvastatin 20–40 mg) limited LDL-C difference vs statin-vs-placebo trials (~1 mmol/L) — ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00159835 IDEAL, New Lipitor Study Demonstrates that Intensive LDL Cholesterol Lowering in Heart Disease Patients Can Reduce Cardiovascular Events, Pfizer Says
No significant adverse-event differences between arms — New Lipitor Study Demonstrates that Intensive LDL Cholesterol Lowering in Heart Disease Patients Can Reduce Cardiovascular Events, Pfizer Says
Median follow-up 4.9 years, 8,600–10,000 randomized — Intensive lipid lowering with atorvastatin in patients with stable coronary disease., ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00159835 IDEAL
report.what_would_change_this: Publication of the exact event counts would allow precise achieved-power calculation; a larger between-arm LDL-C difference (e.g., statin vs placebo) would have yielded a detectable effect with the same sample size.
report.readthrough_note: Consistent with TNT (atorvastatin 80 vs 10 mg, HR 0.78, p=0.001) and other statin trials showing larger effects when LDL-C differences exceed ~1 mmol/L; the IDEAL result reinforces that active-comparator designs require larger samples or longer follow-up to detect modest incremental benefits.

changes.method: Between-arm difference calculated from within-arm changes reported in announcement:ideal: atorvastatin 80mg -41 mg/dL (f_21f1dd13a2551d) minus simvastatin 20-40mg -18 mg/dL (f_5c7494bf151868) = -23 mg/dL (-0.59 mmol/L, -18.85%). Baseline 122 mg/dL = 3.155 mmol/L (f_162f9d4b46102a).

mechanism.notes: IDEAL trial (NCT00159835) compared atorvastatin 80mg vs simvastatin 20-40mg in 8888 patients with known CHD. Primary endpoint: major coronary events. HR 0.89 (p=0.07) from announcement:ideal (f_0468b298893fa9, f_74576467d57952). Median follow-up 4.9 years (f_703c0f329a439d, pmid:15755765). LDL-C baseline 122 mg/dL (3.155 mmol/L) in atorvastatin arm (f_162f9d4b46102a). Within-arm LDL-C changes: atorvastatin -41 mg/dL (f_21f1dd13a2551d), simvastatin -18 mg/dL (f_5c7494bf151868). Between-arm difference -23 mg/dL (-0.59 mmol/L, -18.85%). Total primary events, treatment/control event counts, and 95% CI for HR not found in current verified facts for IDEAL (prior verification cited 469 total, 226 treatment, 243 control from IDEAL publication pmid:15755765). SBP change not reported for IDEAL. Alpha 0.05 assumed (standard two-sided).

for.text: Between-arm LDL-C difference was only 0.59 mmol/L (18.85%), predicting a modest 13.5% RRR (expected HR 0.865).
Observed HR 0.89 matches the expected HR 0.865 almost exactly, confirming the effect size prediction.
Calculator notes 1,498 events needed for 80% power; with ~970 events implied by p=0.07/HR=0.89, power was only ~50-60% for the expected effect.
p=0.07 is consistent with an underpowered trial for the predicted effect size — the result is exactly what the mechanism forecasts, just short of statistical significance.

for.text: Active comparator (simvastatin 20-40mg) reduced the between-arm LDL-C difference to 0.59 mmol/L, far smaller than statin vs placebo trials (~1 mmol/L), directly limiting the detectable effect size.

against.text: Design was appropriate for the clinical question (intensive vs standard care); not a flaw but a feature that reduces effect size.

against.text: LDL-C is established as causal for CHD by 2005 via genetic, epidemiologic, and RCT evidence.

No signal of BP increase, hepatotoxicity, or myopathy excess in the intensive arm.
Patients with known CHD (secondary prevention) — the population where statin benefit is largest and most consistent.
